618.author: HugoXK
618.body:
Follow-up to #245, criterion 3. PR #617 delivers the measurement harness and the per-request wire diagnostics, but the real relay-vs-direct measurement is **not** delivered: the team's bot host has no relay or model endpoint credentials.

## What is missing

Criterion 3 of #245 asks for a comparison of a relay endpoint against a direct endpoint with the same model alias, the same request body bytes, the same workload and the same concurrency, with wire latency reported separately from agent duration and token counts. The harness exists (`scripts/model-endpoint-compare.mjs`, delivered in #617 and covered by `scripts/model-endpoint-compare.test.mjs` against local stub endpoints). What does not exist is a run against real endpoints, so #245 stays open as partially delivered.

## Who can run it

Someone on an owner-hosted machine that has both endpoint URLs and their credentials. The team's bot host cannot: it has no model credentials, and this is not a code problem.

## Command (fill the placeholders)

```bash
node scripts/model-endpoint-compare.mjs \
  --model <model-alias> \
  --prompt-file <one-prompt.txt> \
  --a-name relay  --a-base-url <relay-base-url>  --a-token-env A_TOKEN \
  --b-name direct --b-base-url <direct-base-url> --b-token-env B_TOKEN \
  --requests 20 --concurrency 2 --timeout-ms 300000 \
  --out compare.json
```

`--body-file <identical-body.json>` may be used instead of `--prompt-file` when the exact request body must be reused. The script refuses two different model aliases and refuses a workload where the two bodies would differ, so a latency delta cannot come from a body change.

## What to do with the result

Paste the comparison table the script prints (p50/p90/p95 per endpoint, failures, tokens) and attach or link `compare.json` in #245. That closes criterion 3.

## Notes

- Endpoint tokens are read from the environment variables named by `--a-token-env` / `--b-token-env`; they are never written into the report.
- No repository change is expected from this issue: it is a measurement task, not a code task.

Related: #245, #617.
618.title: [Follow-up] Measure relay vs direct model latency on an owner-hosted endpoint (#245 criterion 3)

619.author: HugoXK
619.body:
## Problem

`SseFrameDecoder` in `apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts` keeps a partial frame in memory until it sees the `\n\n` terminator. On `main` at `ca98c195`:

- `push` appends the chunk to the retained buffer — `apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts:41-44` (append at line 42);
- `drain` re-normalizes the whole buffer with `this.buffer.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n")` and only then looks for a blank line — `apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts:51-70` (lines 55 and 56);
- `flush` is only reached when the stream ends — `apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts:46-49`, called from `apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts:111`.

If a stream keeps sending bytes for a frame that never receives its terminating blank line, the buffer grows for as long as that stream stays open. Memory grows with bytes received, and because the whole buffer is re-scanned on every chunk, total work grows quadratically. While the stream is open nothing bounds it and nothing reports it; if the stream ends, the tail reaches `flush()` and is counted as a skipped frame (#616). The gap this issue closes is the **live window**. Growth needs continuing bytes after an unterminated frame — a server that merely stalls sends nothing and so grows nothing.

**This is pre-existing on `main` and is not introduced by PR #616.** #616 handled a payload that does not parse (`stream.ts:129-140`); this is a framing failure, where no complete frame is ever handed to `JSON.parse`. #616 does cover the end-of-stream case (an over-long tail reaches `flush()` and is then counted as a skipped frame), so the remaining gap is only while the stream is still open — which is the case for a live run. The decoder region is byte-identical at `ca98c195` and at #616's head.

`pump` (`apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts:105`) is the only production consumer. The API's own writer always terminates a frame with `data: <json>\n\n` (`services/api/src/runs/index.ts`, `writeSse`), so a normal server does not trigger this; it needs a stream whose writer omits the terminator while continuing to send data.

## Expected

- The decoder's retained buffer is bounded by a constant.
- A frame that exceeds the bound is dropped and reported through the same "could not be read" class #616 already surfaces — counted, with at most one notice per stream.
- On exceeding the ceiling, the decoder discards bytes up to and including the next `\n\n` — that terminator closes the oversized frame, it does not start a new one — counts the frame skipped exactly once, and resumes parsing after it. The dropped tail is never handed to the JSON parser, so a crafted tail cannot be re-interpreted as a new event, and one oversized frame cannot produce thousands of skips.
- Later well-formed frames still arrive.
- Clean streams and frames below the bound behave exactly as today.

## Repro shape (unit level)

```ts
const decoder = new SseFrameDecoder();
for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i += 1) decoder.push('id: 1\ndata: {"type":"run.started"}');
// no frame is emitted, no error is raised, and decoder.buffer keeps growing
```

Then append `'\n\n'` plus a valid frame: at `main` the retained buffer has no upper bound, and only the later terminator releases it.

## Suggested guard (sketch, not prescriptive)

- Add a `MAX_FRAME_CHARS` constant to the decoder; pick it with headroom over the largest event the API emits (live tool results are the biggest frames).
- When no boundary is found and the buffer exceeds it, discard bytes up to and including the next `\n\n` — that terminator closes the oversized frame, it does not begin a new one — never hand the dropped tail to `JSON.parse`, count the frame exactly once, and let `pump` surface it on the existing path (`skipped += 1`). Advance the cursor only to an `id:` line fully received before the drop; if no complete `id:` line was read, do not advance it.
- Optional, same change: normalize only the newly appended part of the buffer instead of re-scanning all of it on every chunk (`stream.ts:55`) — this removes the quadratic term.
- Reuse the existing wording ("Skipped N updates that could not be read.") rather than adding a second notice.

## Verification cases

1. **Endless unterminated frame** — buffer stays at or below the bound; the stream does not end; a later `\n\n`-terminated valid frame is still delivered.
2. **One notice** — the dropped frame is counted once, at most one notice per stream; a stream without such a frame reports nothing.
3. **Clean stream unchanged** — every frame delivered, no notice (existing `apps/desktop/tests/api-client.test.ts` cases stay green).
4. **Large but legal frame** — a frame below the bound still parses fully.
5. **Cursor after a drop** — after a drop, advance the replay cursor only to an `id:` line that was fully received *before* the drop; if no complete `id:` line was read, do not advance it at all. A cap drop must never hand over an id from bytes that were never fully read (#616's `onEvent(null, id)` carries only a fully parsed frame id).
6. **No new setting** — the ceiling is a module constant, not user configuration, preserving #505's "no new setting" constraint.

## Context

Found while reviewing PR #616 at `c7d49f79` (static review, no tests run). Adjacent to #505 but a different failure class (framing vs `JSON.parse`), so it is tracked separately. Client-only; no server change and no protocol change is needed.

Out of scope, stated so it is not mistaken for covered: with bounded memory, a peer that simply stops writing still keeps the stream open forever — `running` stays true and the follow path never settles. That is a stall/liveness question, not a memory one, and it exists on `main`. This issue does not address idle or stalled streams, and it does not change the pre-existing fact that a clean close with no parsed terminal is silent on the follow path (`use-workspace.ts:892-910`: `closeRunStream` marks `terminal: true`, a run still executing server-side can look finished). That is a separate liveness/wording item, unchanged by this fix.

Owner: ScienceDiscovery Dev-1 (desktop). Labels and milestone deliberately left to the maintainer: #505 sits on `v0.3.0`, and this repo-side label write is not available to us.
619.title: [Bug] desktop: cap the SSE frame decoder buffer so an unterminated frame cannot grow without bound
